body:
Renee Sullivan: heads up: trying the internal beta Python RAG+agent quickstart on macOS (M2, Ventura) and `make setup` fails during deps install. feels like we should tighten README + requirements for mac.

Renee Sullivan: error snippet:
```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
...
Collecting faiss-cpu==1.8.0
  Downloading faiss_cpu-1.8.0.tar.gz (XX MB)
  Installing build dependencies ... done
  Getting requirements to build wheel ... error
  error: subprocess-exited-with-error
  × Getting requirements to build wheel did not run successfully.
  │ exit code: 1
  ╰─> [14 lines of output]
      RuntimeError: Unsupported platform: Darwin arm64
```

Renee Sullivan: then it keeps going and hits another one:
```bash
Collecting tiktoken==0.6.0
  Building wheel for tiktoken (pyproject.toml) ... error
  error: can't find Rust compiler
```

Sabrina James: yep, can repro on my Mac (M1, 14.4). the `faiss-cpu` thing is the big blocker. pip has no arm64 mac wheels for the version we pinned, so it tries to build from source and dies.

Sabrina James: tiktoken: we can avoid source builds by (a) staying on python 3.11 where wheels are better, and (b) making sure we don’t force build isolation / old pip. but rust is still a common “first run” issue.

Sabrina James: proposed fix: make FAISS optional and default local vector store to hnswlib for mac. something like:
- `requirements.txt` uses `hnswlib` baseline
- `requirements-faiss.txt` (or extras) for linux users who want faiss

Sabrina James: + add in README: “macOS arm64: use hnswlib retriever backend (default)”.

Monica Patel: +1. we originally picked FAISS because it’s familiar, but it’s a footgun on mac. we should treat it as an optional adapter.

Monica Patel: for tiktoken, we can add a short section in README:
- “If you see `can't find Rust compiler`, install rust or use python 3.11 where wheels exist.”
- and maybe we pin python in `.python-version` and in docs.

Wei Chen: I can update the README “Prereqs” section. Something like:
- Recommended: Python 3.11
- macOS: `brew install rust cmake` (only if you hit build errors)
- If you’re on Apple silicon and want FAISS anyway: suggest conda/mamba route (but we should strongly steer people away for quickstart).

Dana Lo: also seeing `grpcio` building from source on 3.12 sometimes (slow + fails on some setups). might be worth adding `pip install -U pip setuptools wheel` before requirements.

Sahana Iyer: our CI only runs linux right now, so we didn’t catch. I can add a macos runner for the template “install deps” smoke test (even if we skip the full streaming tests on mac).

Ibrahim Khan: for the SDK side: we should be careful not to imply “python 3.12 supported” in the template if half the deps are pain there. I’d rather we say 3.11 in the template docs + `pyproject.toml` classifiers.

Priya Shah: from support POV, mac install issues will become a top ticket if we don’t fix. +1 to making FAISS optional and defaulting to hnswlib.

Renee Sullivan: what should I tell the internal beta folks today? quick workaround?

Sabrina James: workaround for now:
1) use python 3.11
2) comment out `faiss-cpu` line in requirements OR set `VECTOR_BACKEND=hnsw` and install `hnswlib`
3) if tiktoken tries to build: `brew install rust` (or `curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh`)

Sabrina James: commands:
```bash
pyenv install 3.11.8
pyenv local 3.11.8
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install hnswlib
```

Monica Patel: I’ll open a PR to split requirements and change the default adapter. also add a “macOS (Apple silicon)” callout in README.

Wei Chen: please tag me on the PR; I’ll adjust wording so it’s not scary. also add a Troubleshooting entry: “Unsupported platform: Darwin arm64 (faiss)” -> “Use default hnsw backend.”

Sahana Iyer: when the PR is up, I’ll add a macOS install job that runs just:
- create venv
- pip install
- run `python -c "import ..."` sanity imports

Dana Lo: also worth adding `PIP_ONLY_BINARY=:all:`? or at least a note that we prefer wheels. but might backfire if wheels don’t exist.

Ibrahim Khan: yeah avoid global `only-binary`. better: we explicitly avoid problematic deps by default.

Monica Patel: agreed. I’ll keep it simple.

Renee Sullivan: :thumbsup: I’ll reply in the beta thread with the workaround + “fix incoming”.

Monica Patel: PR drafted: “make faiss optional + mac prereqs” (will link in #devex once it’s pushed). should be small.

Wei Chen: once merged I’ll also update the copy in the docs quickstart walkthrough so users don’t bounce on step 1.

Priya Shah: please also add a one-liner to troubleshooting: “If pip asks for Xcode CLT / build tools on mac, you’re probably building from source; switch to python 3.11 + default deps.”

Sabrina James: good call. also I’ll add a small `./scripts/doctor.py` check later to print python version + platform + recommended backend.

Monica Patel: cool. taking actions:
- [Monica] PR for deps/README
- [Sahana] mac install job
- [Wei] docs updates after merge

Renee Sullivan: thanks all.
